page: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-1g is an accelerator-optimized instance configured for deep learning training, large language model inference, and high-performance computing. The host platform pairs one NVIDIA A100 GPU equipped with 80 GB of high-bandwidth memory with an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The compute allocation provides 12 vCPUs across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, alongside 170 GB of system memory, yielding an expansive host-memory-to-vCPU ratio of over 14 GB per core. The instance also provisions 402 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark measurements highlight clear architectural specialization. In GPU-driven machine learning workloads, the server achieves top-tier inference speeds across small, medium, and large model architectures. Text generation reaches 146.79 tokens per second on 7B parameter models and 24.47 tokens per second on 70B parameter models, with prompt ingestion reaching 499.41 tokens per second on 70B workloads. Conversely, host CPU single-thread performance places in the lower percentile with a Geekbench single-core score of 1058.0 and a stress-ng score of 1200.99, while multi-core compute and system memory bandwidth fall within median ranges.

The qualitative trade-off of the a2-ultragpu-1g reflects its focus on accelerator-bound tasks. Allocating high host memory and dedicated 80 GB GPU VRAM creates a specialized compute footprint where CPU-bound processing, general compilation, or sequential operations are secondary. The instance provides strong resource efficiency when applied directly to tensor-based computations, distributed neural network tasks, batch inference pipelines, and scientific data modeling where host-to-device streaming and GPU memory density are primary constraints.
description: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-1g is an accelerator-optimized virtual machine engineered for GPU-intensive workloads, including large language model inference and deep learning. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at 2.2 GHz, it features 12 vCPUs (6 physical cores), 170 GB of system memory, and 402 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The primary computing resource is a dedicated NVIDIA A100 GPU with 80 GB of high-bandwidth memory. In benchmark evaluations, the instance delivers top-tier performance for transformer model inference across 7B and 70B parameter models, while general-purpose single-core and multi-core CPU metrics remain in the lower and median tiers respectively. With substantial host RAM and bundled NVMe scratch space, the instance provides strong resource alignment for machine learning serving, scientific simulations, and large-scale data modeling.
